systems.name: 3.1 Prop Mode (Object Disguise)
systems.notes: The Mimic can possess any non-player object (chests, crates, torches). While in Prop Mode, the Mimic is invulnerable but immobile. Must be able to observe surroundings.
tasks: Implement object possession: click on object to inhabit it
Prop Mode: invulnerable, immobile, can observe nearby area
Visual: subtle tell on possessed object (slight shimmer or eye)
Object physics: Mimic exits Prop Mode, object returns to normal

systems.name: 3.2 Infiltration Mode (Player Disguise)
systems.notes: After eliminating a player, the Mimic can assume their identity. Gains access to that character's inventory, abilities, and appearance. Vulnerable to damage and Spirit Checks.
tasks: On player kill: Mimic can absorb identity (inventory, abilities, sprite)
Infiltration Mode: Mimic is vulnerable, must act convincingly
Cooldown on ability use while disguised (can't spam victim's skills)
Disguise degrades over time: subtle visual tells appear

systems.name: 3.3 Mimic Hunting & Elimination
systems.notes: The Mimic eliminates players through ambushes. Transition from Prop → attack → Infiltration should feel fluid and rewarding.
tasks: Ambush attack: high damage when attacking from Prop Mode
Sustained damage in open combat (lower than ambush)
Elimination animation: player dragged into shadows
Trophy collected: skull added to Trophy Room

systems.name: 3.4 Mimic Progression & Learning
systems.notes: The Mimic learns player tactics over the campaign. Unlocks new abilities or perks based on skulls collected and patterns observed.
tasks: Track player behaviours: common routes, item usage, communication patterns
Unlock Mimic perks at skull milestones (e.g., faster transition, silent kill)
Mimic XP system: earn points for successful eliminations
Perk tree: stealth, deception, combat branches
